lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing, Python
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Projects should appear before Experience to surface product-related work before the Diesel Mechanic role.
items.because: The app is product-related, while the Diesel Mechanic role is not closely connected to the apparent product direction.

items.says: Experience should appear above Education for a candidate with five years of post-degree work.
items.because: Leading with Education delays the more relevant work evidence.

items.says: The bullet uses a personal pronoun and passive phrasing.
items.because: “My” reads like a sentence, and the passive construction obscures who rolled out the redesign and retrained the pickers.

items.says: “Sizing the loss by segment” does not state the analysis’s finding.
items.because: A reader cannot assess the opportunity’s scale or how the analysis informed the business case.

items.says: “Set the next quarter’s roadmap priority” does not identify the priority or what changed.
items.because: A reader cannot see the decision’s result or practical value.

items.says: The checkout test and conversion lift repeat the result in an earlier Harbor Payments bullet.
items.because: A reader may count the repeated lift as a second achievement.

items.says: The Harbor Payments bullets repeat the roadmap-prioritization result.
items.because: Reporting the prioritization twice makes the experience seem repetitive rather than showing a distinct contribution.

items.says: The line does not establish that the scorecards or renegotiations caused late deliveries to fall.
items.because: A before-and-after rate alone cannot show causation without consistent definitions and comparable shipment data.

items.says: The 30% pick-error reduction lacks an error measure or denominator.
items.because: Error counts and rates can change differently as volume changes.

items.says: The 30% pick-error reduction gives no baseline rates or comparison period.
items.because: A reader cannot assess the starting error level or how long the comparison covers.

items.says: The forecast-error claim does not identify the error metric or forecast horizon.
items.because: The figures are comparable only if they use the same metric, horizon and scope.

items.says: The 1,800-hour annual saving lacks a measurement method and clear attribution.
items.because: The claim needs actual time data and a defensible estimate that accounts for workload and service levels.

items.says: The long intervention list buries the result and leaves “which saved” without a clear referent.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which action the saving refers to.

items.says: Redistribution does not establish that the 9 tonnes of food would otherwise have been thrown away.
items.because: The pickups do not show what would have happened to the food otherwise.

items.says: The launch does not identify a product or operational decision you personally led.
items.because: The line gives the outcome and scale but not the skill behind the launch.

items.says: The increase from 400 to 1,150 weekly active users is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: The increase is 750 users, or 187.5% of the original 400.

items.says: The fill-rate change is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: A rise from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points; the relative increase is approximately 26.7%.

items.says: The $2.4M annual saving estimate does not identify its comparison or basis.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the projected saving represents or how the model produced it.

items.says: The practicum bullets repeat that the scheduling pilot was approved or funded.
items.because: Repeating the client decision takes space from the savings case and presentation.
